_comment: Performance budgets, in gzipped KB as GitHub Pages serves them.
`ceiling` fails the check — it is today's value plus a little headroom, so nothing regresses.
`target` is where docs/INVARIANTS.md says we are going; it is reported, not enforced.
When a phase lands and the real number drops below `target`, LOWER the ceiling to the new
value + headroom in the same commit. That is how the ratchet works — a budget that is never
tightened is a budget that is never met.

boot.why: Everything needed to paint the hero and the first 25 cards. INTENT-2 (speed is the product).

search.why: Everything that must land before a text query can be answered. The single biggest lever on felt speed — see PERF-UX-AUDIT-2026-09-14.md S1 and E1. T1 dropped the sl field (-206 KB); T3 split questions.json into qmeta.json+qtext.json (no byte change by itself, but questions.json is no longer fetched by fresh app.js, so it's replaced here by its two successors — it stays deployed for one release as a compat shim for a cached pre-T3 app.js, tracked separately in docs/DECISIONS.md, not in this budget). Measured 1728.2 KB after T1+T3; ceiling carries ~55 KB headroom for corpus growth between sessions. Phase 5's inverted index is what reaches the 800 KB target.

app_js.why: DECISION-2 (no framework, no bundler). If this creeps past ~28 KB gz, something was added that probably belongs in a lazy-loaded module.
